q: In the Bahay Kubo, what purpose do the spaced Bamboo Slats (Floor) serve, aside from allowing air to rise through the house?
o: They act as thermal mass to store heat
They prevent any airflow into the living space
They are used exclusively for structural support of the roof
They provide an easy way to clean by sweeping dust directly below
n: Bamboo Slats (Floor) are spaced flooring that allows air to rise through the house and provides an easy way to clean by sweeping dust directly below.

q: Which heat transfer process is the transfer of heat energy from one vibrating molecule to the one immediately adjacent to it, without relative displacement of the molecules, taking place within or between solid bodies?
o: Conduction
Radiation
Emissivity
Convection
n: Conduction is the process in which heat energy is transferred from one vibrating molecule to the one immediately adjacent to it without any relative displacement of the molecules. This process takes place within or between solid bodies.

s: Thermal Forces — Air Entry and Escape
q: Due to thermal forces, where does air enter and escape a building?
o: Air enters through the lower-level openings of a building and escapes through openings located at higher portions of the building
Air enters through upper-level openings and escapes through lower-level openings
Air only enters through the roof
Air enters and escapes through the same single opening
n: Due to thermal forces, air enters a building through the lower-level openings and escapes through openings located at higher portions of the building.

q: What is a Brise-Soleil?
o: A solid or louvered panel that can be closed over windows
An adjustable window covering that can be tilted to control light and privacy
A mesh or fabric installed over windows to reduce solar heat gain while maintaining visibility
A permanent architectural feature, such as a horizontal or vertical louver, designed to block direct sunlight
n: A Brise-Soleil is a permanent architectural feature, such as a horizontal or vertical louver, designed to block direct sunlight.

q: What is meant by 'Structural Independence' in the Bahay na Bato's seismic and thermal innovations?
o: The house utilizes a post-and-lintel timber frame supporting the upper floor and roof, with a stone ground floor (arquitectura mestiza) that is often non-load bearing for the upper levels, allowing the wooden structure to sway during earthquakes without collapsing
The house has no ground floor at all
The timber frame and stone floor are structurally fused into a single rigid unit
The stone ground floor bears the full structural load of the entire house
n: Structural Independence: the Bahay na Bato utilizes a post-and-lintel timber frame that supports the upper floor and roof. The stone ground floor (arquitectura mestiza) is often non-load bearing for the upper levels, allowing the wooden structure to sway during earthquakes without collapsing.

q: Regarding the two important aspects of radiation, what is Emissivity?
o: The average solar radiation received outside Earth's atmosphere
The ability of a material to give off thermal radiation
The capacity of a material to absorb radiant energy and convert it to other forms of energy
The vertical angle between the sun and the horizon
n: Emissivity is the ability of a material to give off thermal radiation. All materials emit heat; however, this varies in degree. Most building materials are good emitters of thermal radiation, but highly polished surfaces have low emissivity.

q: What is the Partition Effect, as described in the source?
o: Partitions have no measurable effect on airflow patterns
A partition always blocks all airflow regardless of its orientation
A partition perpendicular to the wind always increases airflow
A partition placed parallel to the main flow of air has minimal influence on the pattern of air flow, but one placed perpendicular to the incident wind creates a wind shadow
n: Partition Effect: when a partition is placed parallel to the main flow of air, this has minimal influence on the pattern of air flow; but when located perpendicular to the incident wind, this creates a wind shadow.

q: What defines the Windward Side of a building?
o: The side where air always exits during cross ventilation
The side facing into the wind, where wind first hits the building; it experiences higher air pressure and is typically cooler and more ventilated
The side facing true south regardless of wind direction
The side sheltered from the wind, experiencing lower air pressure and calmer air
n: The windward side is the side facing into the wind. This is where the wind first hits a building or structure. It experiences higher air pressure and is typically cooler and more ventilated.

q: Why were Capiz shells used as window material in the Bahay na Bato?
o: They are the only material capable of transmitting sunlight
They serve solely a decorative role with no functional purpose
They are durable enough to withstand the typhoon rains and winds
They provide the same thermal mass function as a Trombe wall
n: Capiz shells are durable enough to withstand the typhoon rains and winds.

q: What is the Solar Constant?
o: A device that absorbs solar radiation and transfers heat to a fluid
The average solar radiation received outside Earth's atmosphere, approximately 1361 W/m²
A system using solar energy to heat air or water for residential or commercial use
A house designed to harness solar energy for heating, lighting, or power
n: The Solar Constant is the average solar radiation received outside Earth's atmosphere, approximately 1361 W/m².

q: According to PAGASA, what is the Philippine Southwest Monsoon season, occurring from June to October, characterized by frequent heavy rainfall, storms, and typhoons?
o: Hot Dry Season
Amihan
Tag-init
Habagat
n: Habagat (Southwest Monsoon) occurs from June to October and is characterized by frequent heavy rainfall, storms, and typhoons.

q: Regarding Walls as a basic element of an energy efficient building, why should tropical buildings avoid facing the East-West direction?
o: Because the building absorbs more heat in that orientation
Because it eliminates cross ventilation entirely
Because it increases construction costs only
Because it reduces available window area
n: For walls, construction orientation should be analyzed based on the sun path. In tropical countries, the building should avoid facing the East-West direction because the building absorbs more heat.

s: Passive Cooling — Shading and Media Aguas
q: According to the source, what do deep roof overhangs and window awnings ensure, under the principle of Shading and Media Aguas?
o: That the building envelope maximizes solar heat absorption
That the building self-shades, preventing the building envelope from absorbing solar heat
That the roof ridge is sealed to prevent any airflow
That windows can be completely eliminated from the design
n: Shading and Media Aguas: Deep roof overhangs and window awnings ensure that the building self-shades, preventing the building envelope from absorbing solar heat.

q: What is Passive Solar Heating?
o: A device that absorbs solar radiation and transfers the heat to a fluid
A system that uses mechanical equipment like pumps or fans to circulate heat-transfer fluids
The average solar radiation received outside Earth's atmosphere
A method that utilizes building orientation, materials, and thermal mass to collect and distribute heat naturally
n: Passive Solar Heating utilizes building orientation, materials, and thermal mass to collect and distribute heat naturally.

q: According to the source's discussion of wind patterns, what does Habagat bring?
o: Cold air only during winter solstice
Cool, dry air from the northeast
No measurable wind
Warm, moist air from the southwest, bringing heavier rains and humidity
n: Habagat brings warm, moist air from the southwest, resulting in heavier rains and humidity.

q: Regarding the Roof as a basic element of an energy efficient building, what treatment is recommended after the roof, along with using light-colored roofs?
o: Painting the roof a dark color for maximum absorption
Removing all roof overhangs
Adding heavy dense roofing materials
Putting insulation with reflective foil
n: For the roof, considerations include the materials used (cement, tiles, metal sheets, etc.), the way it is built/designed, the mass of the roof, putting insulation with reflective foil after the roof, and using light-colored roofs.

q: Which term describes the height of the sun above the horizon — the vertical angle between the sun and the horizon at a given moment?
o: Longitude
Meridian
Azimuth
Altitude
n: Altitude is the height above the horizon — the vertical angle between the sun and the horizon at a given moment; higher angles occur in summer.

q: Which atmospheric circulation cell (0°–30° latitude) is characterized by warm air rising at the equator, moving toward 30° latitude, then cooling and sinking to create subtropical high-pressure zones (deserts)?
o: Hadley Cell
Ferrel Cell
Trade Wind Cell
Polar Cell
n: The Hadley Cell (0°–30° latitude) has warm air rising at the equator and moving toward 30° latitude, where it cools and sinks, creating subtropical high-pressure zones (deserts).

q: According to the source's Passive Systems table, which combination describes the hot-humid climate strategy?
o: Minimum radiant heat gain, moderate wind resistance, moderate internal airflow
Moderate thermal retention, moderate radiant heat gain, slight wind exposure
Maximum thermal retention, maximum radiant heat gain, maximum wind resistance
Maximum wind exposure, maximum internal airflow, minimum radiant heat gain
n: For a hot-humid climate, passive systems call for maximum wind exposure, maximum internal airflow, and minimum radiant heat gain.

q: What is Stack Ventilation / Chimney Effect?
o: A principle relying entirely on wind pressure differences between building sides
A principle used exclusively for cooling roof materials
A method that only works during daytime, never at night
A principle that draws cool air in from low openings while letting warm air escape through high-level openings, using the fact that warm air rises due to its lower density
n: Warm air rises due to its lower density. Stack ventilation uses this principle to draw cool air from low openings while letting warm air escape through high-level openings like clerestory windows or roof vents. Stack ventilation works even without wind, driven purely by indoor-outdoor temperature differences, and is particularly useful at night or in urban areas where outdoor air movement is restricted. It is best combined with thermal mass and good insulation for enhanced performance.

q: According to the source, why does the angle of the sun get lower the farther a location is from the equator?
o: Because meridians converge near the equator
Because azimuth angles only apply near the tropics
Because the earth's longitude decreases toward the poles
Because the sun's rays strike the convex surface of the earth more obliquely
n: The farther away from the equator, the lower the angle of the sun, because the sun's rays strike the convex surface of the earth more obliquely.

q: According to the source's Principles of Air Flow, what happens because 'air possesses inertia'?
o: Air always flows in a perfectly straight line regardless of obstacles
Once set in motion, air tends to continue to flow in its initial direction until some interviewing (intervening) force is met
Air stops moving the instant it encounters any obstacle
Air loses all momentum immediately upon entering a building
n: Air possesses inertia. Once set in motion, it tends to continue to flow in its initial direction until some intervening force is met.

q: What is a Berm, as a passive solar design element?
o: A mound or bank of earth used in landscaping for insulation, privacy, or to direct water flow
A thermal mass wall, often cylindrical, designed to absorb and store solar heat
An outdoor platform designed to receive ample sunlight
A room with extensive glass surfaces designed to capture sunlight for warmth and light
n: A Berm is a mound or bank of earth used in landscaping for insulation, privacy, or to direct water flow.

q: According to the source, Philippine vernacular architecture is defined by its ability to adapt to what kind of environment?
o: A temperate environment with four distinct seasons
A high-humidity, high-temperature, and seismically active maritime environment
A cold, dry, seismically inactive environment
A desert environment with minimal rainfall
n: Philippine vernacular architecture is defined by its ability to adapt to a high-humidity, high-temperature, and seismically active maritime environment. Rather than resisting the elements with heavy mass, traditional structures utilize lightweight materials and permeability to achieve thermal comfort and structural resilience.

q: What is the Winter Solstice?
o: The day when the sun reaches its lowest point in the sky at noon, resulting in the shortest day of the year, typically around December 21 in the Northern Hemisphere
A day when day and night are approximately equal in length
The day when the sun reaches its highest point in the sky at noon
The average solar radiation received outside Earth's atmosphere
n: The Winter Solstice is the day when the sun reaches its lowest point in the sky at noon, resulting in the shortest day of the year, typically around December 21 in the Northern Hemisphere.

q: What is a Land Breeze?
o: The result of the Ferrel Cell
Wind that develops during the day, moving from sea to land
A wind pattern unique to mountainous regions only
Wind that develops at night when the land cools faster than the water, resulting in air movement from land to sea at the surface and from sea to land upward
n: A Land Breeze occurs at night: the land cools faster than the water, and the resulting movement of air is from land to sea at the surface, and from sea to land upward.

q: What is a Sun Deck?
o: A room with extensive glass surfaces designed to capture sunlight
An outdoor platform designed to receive ample sunlight, often used for relaxation or solar access
A mound or bank of earth used for insulation, privacy, or to direct water flow
A thick wall painted dark and faced with glass
n: A Sun Deck is an outdoor platform designed to receive ample sunlight, often used for relaxation or solar access.

q: In the Bahay Kubo, what is the function of Thatch Roofing made of nipa or anahaw?
o: It eliminates the need for any window openings
It is designed to absorb and store maximum solar heat
It is used only for decorative, non-functional purposes
The air pockets within the thatch act as a natural thermal insulator, preventing solar heat from radiating into the interior
n: Thatch Roofing is steeply pitched and made of nipa or anahaw. The air pockets within the thatch act as a natural thermal insulator, preventing solar heat from radiating into the interior.

q: Which heat transfer process is the transfer of heat between a surface and a moving fluid, by movement of the molecules from one point in a fluid to another, and can be either natural or forced?
o: Radiation
Conduction
Convection
Absorptivity
n: Convection is the transfer of heat between a surface and a moving fluid, or the transfer of heat by movement of the molecules from one point in a fluid to another. Convection can either be natural or forced.

q: At what window height are window heights significant for effective indoor air movement, according to the source?
o: 3.00 meters
0.50 meters
1.10 meters
2.00 meters
n: Window heights are significant for effective indoor air movement when those measure up to 1.10 meters. No additional benefit for direct occupancy comfort is derived if openings are higher, though higher openings can reduce heat loads on the ceiling.

q: What is a Shutter Blind?
o: An adjustable window covering that can be tilted to control light and privacy
A permanent architectural feature designed to block direct sunlight
A mesh or fabric installed over windows to reduce solar heat gain
A device or structure that blocks or filters sunlight to reduce heat gain and glare
n: A Shutter Blind is an adjustable window covering that can be tilted to control light and privacy.

q: What is 'The Volada' in the Bahay na Bato?
o: Pierced wooden panels above doors or walls that allow light and air to circulate
An overhanging gallery that protects the ground floor from rain and direct sun, while also acting as a circulation path that allows air to wrap around the main living rooms
Sliding panels located beneath the main window sills
A latticework panel framing translucent capiz shells
n: The Volada is an overhanging gallery that protects the ground floor from rain and direct sun, while also acting as a circulation path that allows air to wrap around the main living rooms.

q: What is Absorptivity, the second important aspect of radiation discussed in the source?
o: The average solar radiation received outside Earth's atmosphere
The ability of a material to give off thermal radiation
The height of the sun above the horizon
The capacity of a material to absorb radiant energy and convert it to other forms of energy — most construction materials, regardless of color, act as a 'black body'
n: Absorptivity is the capacity of a material to absorb radiant energy and convert it to other forms of energy. Most construction materials, regardless of color, act as a 'black body.' Most thermal radiation the material intercepts is absorbed.

q: According to the source, what is the average temperature range characterizing the Philippines' tropical maritime climate?
n: The Philippines has an average temperature of 25°C to 32°C (77°F to 89°F) — hot and humid throughout the year, with very little variation. The warmest months are typically March to May (dry season peak).

q: What defines the Leeward Side of a building?
o: The side facing into the wind where wind first hits the structure
The side sheltered from the wind, or opposite the wind's direction; it experiences lower air pressure and often calmer air, and air tends to exit from this side during cross ventilation
The side facing true north regardless of wind direction
The side that always has the highest air pressure
n: The leeward side is the side sheltered from the wind, or opposite the wind's direction. It experiences lower air pressure and often calmer air. Air tends to exit from this side during cross ventilation.

q: What is Calado in the Bahay na Bato?
o: A sliding panel located beneath the main window sill
A latticework panel that frames capiz shells to seal windows completely
Pierced wooden panels above doors or walls of each room that allow light and air to circulate in the house
An overhanging gallery that circulates air around the main living rooms
n: Calado are pierced wooden panels above doors or walls of each room that allow light and air to circulate in the house.

q: What is a Solar House?
o: The average solar radiation received outside Earth's atmosphere
A device that absorbs solar radiation and transfers the heat to a fluid
A system using solar energy to heat air or water for residential or commercial use
A house designed to harness solar energy for heating, lighting, or power
n: A Solar House is a house designed to harness solar energy for heating, lighting, or power.

q: According to PAGASA's seasons, what is the Hot Dry Season (Tag-init), and when does it occur?
o: March to May
June to October, wet and stormy
November to February, cool and dry
December to February only
n: Hot Dry Season (Tag-init) occurs from March to May.

q: Regarding Walls in an energy efficient building, why should heavy/dense construction materials generally be avoided?
o: They are always more expensive than lightweight materials
They absorb heat and release it at a very slow pace, resulting in heat gain and heat retention
They prevent all forms of ventilation
They cannot support a roof structure
n: Heavy/dense wall materials should be avoided because they absorb heat and release it at a very slow pace, which results in heat gain and heat retention.

q: Which geographic coordinate specifies east-west position and is used with latitude to determine solar position?
o: Latitude
Meridian
Longitude
Azimuth
n: Longitude is a geographic coordinate specifying east-west position; used with latitude to determine solar position.

q: What is a Solar Collector?
o: The average solar radiation received outside Earth's atmosphere
A device that absorbs solar radiation and transfers the heat to a fluid
A house designed to harness solar energy for heating, lighting, or power
A system using solar energy to heat air or water
n: A Solar Collector is a device that absorbs solar radiation and transfers the heat to a fluid.

q: According to the source, which Philippine areas are noted as having cooler regional microclimates due to elevation?
o: Baguio or Tagaytay
Metro Manila
Bicol and Eastern Visayas
Central Luzon
n: Cooler climates occur in elevated areas like Baguio or Tagaytay, while hotter, drier zones occur in areas like Central Luzon, and more rainfall occurs on eastern-facing coasts (e.g., Bicol, Eastern Visayas) due to exposure to trade winds.

q: Regarding the Floor as a basic element of an energy efficient building, what material property should floor materials have?
o: High density regardless of material type
Materials must always be timber, never concrete
Low emissivity and no infiltration of hot air
High emissivity and high infiltration of hot air
n: For the floor, the type of material used is usually concrete or timber, and materials of low emissivity and no infiltration of hot air should be used.

q: Which term describes the position of the sun with respect to its projection on a horizontal plane, measured from true south and running clockwise?
o: Azimuth
Latitude
Altitude
Longitude
n: Azimuth is the position of the sun with respect to its projection on a horizontal plane. This is measured from true south and running clockwise.

q: Which atmospheric circulation cell (30°–60° latitude) has air flowing poleward near the surface and equatorward at high altitudes, and is less thermally driven, being more influenced by adjacent cells?
o: Ferrel Cell
Trade Wind Cell
Polar Cell
Hadley Cell
n: The Ferrel Cell (30°–60° latitude) has air flowing poleward near the surface and equatorward at high altitudes. It is less thermally driven and more influenced by adjacent cells.

q: According to the source's Passive Systems table, which combination describes the hot-dry climate strategy?
o: Maximum thermal retention and maximum radiant heat gain
Maximum wind exposure and maximum internal airflow
Minimum radiant heat gain, moderate wind resistance, moderate internal airflow
Moderate thermal retention, moderate radiant heat gain, slight wind exposure
n: For a hot-dry climate, passive systems call for minimum radiant heat gain, moderate wind resistance, and moderate internal airflow.

q: According to the source, how can Stack Ventilation be physically achieved in a building's design?
o: By sealing all low-level openings and using only high-level vents
By removing all vertical shafts and stairwells
By including low-level inlets (like windows near the floor) and high-level outlets (like roof vents, clerestories, or solar chimneys), and using light wells or atriums with high exhaust openings
By using only mechanical fans, never passive openings
n: Stack ventilation can be achieved by including low-level inlets (like windows near the floor) and high-level outlets (like roof vents, clerestories, or solar chimneys). Light wells or atriums with high exhaust openings can be used; in taller buildings, this can be amplified with vertical shafts or stairwells.

q: What latitude value is designated to the equator, and what latitude is the North Pole?
o: 1 deg. and 180 deg. N
0 deg. and 180 deg. N
0 deg. and 90 deg. N
1 deg. and 90 deg. N
n: The equator is designated 1 deg. latitude while the north pole is at 90 deg. N latitude.

s: Principles of Air Flow — Least Resistance
q: According to the source's third Principle of Air Flow, which path does air flow through?
o: The path of least resistance
A completely random path
The path of greatest resistance
A path determined solely by temperature, not pressure
n: Air flows through the path of least resistance.

q: What is a Drum Wall?
o: A mound or bank of earth used for insulation or privacy
An outdoor platform designed to receive ample sunlight
A passive solar building feature consisting of a thick wall painted dark and faced with glass
A thermal mass wall, often cylindrical, designed to absorb and store solar heat during the day and release it at night
n: A Drum Wall is a thermal mass wall, often cylindrical, designed to absorb and store solar heat during the day and release it at night.

q: In the Bahay Kubo (Nipa Hut), what are the Haligi?
o: Woven bamboo or rattan panels that permit air filtration
Steeply pitched roofs made of nipa or anahaw
Massive wooden trunks or bamboo poles that elevate the living area, protecting against dampness, seasonal flooding, and pests while allowing sub-floor ventilation
Spaced flooring that allows air to rise through the house
n: Haligi are massive wooden trunks or bamboo poles that elevate the living area. This protects against dampness, seasonal flooding, and pests while allowing for sub-floor ventilation.

q: What is an Equinox?
o: The shortest day of the year in the Northern Hemisphere
The longest day of the year in the Northern Hemisphere
The average solar radiation received outside Earth's atmosphere
A day, occurring twice a year, when day and night are approximately equal in length, around March 21 (vernal) and September 23 (autumnal)
n: An Equinox occurs twice a year when day and night are approximately equal in length, around March 21 (vernal equinox) and September 23 (autumnal equinox).

q: Regarding wind force in building interiors, what pressure condition does the windward side of a building experience compared to the leeward side?
o: The windward side has positive high pressure, while the leeward side has negative pressure
Pressure differences only matter for stack ventilation, not wind
Both sides always have equal pressure
The windward side has negative pressure while the leeward side has positive pressure
n: An important characteristic of wind force is that the windward side has a positive high pressure, while the leeward side has a negative pressure.

q: What is a Sunshade, as a device for solar control in buildings?
o: A mesh or fabric installed over windows to reduce solar heat gain while maintaining visibility
A device or structure that blocks or filters sunlight to reduce heat gain and glare
A solid or louvered panel that can be closed over windows to control light and heat
A permanent architectural feature such as a horizontal or vertical louver designed to block direct sunlight
n: A Sunshade is a device or structure that blocks or filters sunlight to reduce heat gain and glare.

q: In the Bahay na Bato, how was the living platform protected from the damp ground?
o: It was elevated from the damp ground by a stone on the ground floor
It relied on a concrete slab foundation
It was built directly on the ground with no elevation
It was elevated using only bamboo poles, as in the Bahay Kubo
n: The Bahay na Bato's living platform was elevated from the damp ground by a stone on the ground floor.

q: According to the source, what happens during natural convection when fluid comes in contact with a heat source?
o: The fluid is transferred by molecule-to-molecule contact only
The fluid stops moving entirely
The fluid absorbs heat, expands, becomes less dense and rises, causing a natural circulation as cooler fluid moves in to replace it
The fluid immediately sinks and becomes denser
n: Natural convection occurs when fluid comes in contact with a heat source: it absorbs heat, expands, becomes less dense, and rises, allowing a cooler portion of the fluid to meet the heat source, which in turn rises and causes a natural circulation. When air is blown against the surface of a hot fluid, it cools fast.

q: According to the source, how should louvers, slats, and overhangs used as wind deflectors be positioned to redirect air motion onto the occupancy zones of buildings?
o: They should not be angled at all
At a higher level
Only on the roof
At a lower level, close to the floor
n: Louvers, slats, and overhangs should be positioned at a higher level to redirect air motion onto the occupancy zones of buildings.

q: What is a Solar Screen?
o: A mesh or fabric installed over windows to reduce solar heat gain while maintaining visibility
A solid or louvered panel that can be closed over windows to control light and heat
A permanent architectural feature, such as a horizontal or vertical louver, designed to block direct sunlight
An outdoor platform designed to receive ample sunlight
n: A Solar Screen is a mesh or fabric installed over windows to reduce solar heat gain while maintaining visibility.

q: What are Ventanillas in the Bahay na Bato?
o: Latticework panels framed with translucent capiz shells
Pierced wooden panels above doors that allow light and air to circulate
A thick, dark-painted glass wall that absorbs solar heat
Sliding panels located beneath the main window sills, protected by rejas (iron grilles), allowing low-level air intake even when main windows are closed for privacy or during rain
n: Ventanillas are sliding panels located beneath the main window sills. They are protected by rejas (iron grilles) and allow for low-level air intake even when main windows are closed for privacy or during rain.

q: What is a 'black body' as described in the source's discussion of absorptivity?
o: An ideal material which can absorb radiation with the highest possible emittance
A material used only for solar collectors
A material that reflects all radiant energy
A material with the lowest possible emittance
n: The black body is an ideal material which can absorb radiation with the highest possible emittance.

q: According to the source, what is the relative humidity range in the Philippines, especially high during the rainy season?
o: 90% to 100% year-round
n: Relative humidity in the Philippines ranges from 70% to 90%, and is especially high during the rainy season.

q: What does Bernoulli's Principle explain, as applied to architecture?
o: That wind direction is unaffected by nearby structures, vegetation, or terrain
That air pressure remains constant regardless of speed
That warm air always sinks while cool air always rises

That as air flows faster, its pressure drops — air higher above the ground, with fewer obstacles, typically moves more quickly and has lower pressure, a difference that can help pull fresh air through a building
n: Bernoulli's principle is a fundamental concept in fluid dynamics explaining how differences in wind speed can drive air movement. As air flows faster, its pressure drops. In architecture, air higher above the ground — where there are fewer obstacles — typically moves more quickly and has lower pressure; this pressure difference can help pull fresh air through a building. Nearby structures, vegetation, or terrain can block or channel this airflow.

q: According to the source's Passive Cooling Principles for Modern Application, along which axis should the long axis of a building run, and why?
o: North to South, to maximize morning and afternoon sun exposure
It does not matter, since orientation has no effect on solar heat gain
East to West, to minimize the wall surface area exposed to the low-angle morning and afternoon sun while maximizing the facade's ability to catch prevailing Amihan and Habagat winds
Diagonally at 45 degrees to the compass, for aesthetic reasons only
n: Building Orientation: Strategic placement is critical. The long axis of the building should run from East to West. This minimizes the wall surface area exposed to the low-angle morning and afternoon sun while maximizing the facade's ability to catch the prevailing Amihan (Northeast) and Habagat (Southwest) winds.

q: What is a Solar-Heating System?
o: A system using solar energy to heat air or water for residential or commercial use
A house designed to harness solar energy for heating, lighting, or power
Utilizes building orientation, materials, and thermal mass to collect and distribute heat naturally
A device that absorbs solar radiation and transfers heat to a fluid
n: A Solar-Heating System is a system using solar energy to heat air or water for residential or commercial use.

q: According to the source, approximately how many typhoons enter the Philippine Area of Responsibility (PAR) annually, and how many typically make landfall?
o: An average of 5 typhoons enters the PAR annually; 1–2 make landfall
An average of 2 typhoons enters the PAR annually; none make landfall
An average of 20 typhoons enters the PAR annually; 8–10 make landfall
An average of 50 typhoons enters the PAR annually; 30 make landfall
n: An average of 20 typhoons enters the Philippine Area of Responsibility annually; 8–10 of these make landfall. The most active typhoon months are July to October.

q: Regarding Windows in an energy efficient building, how does window area relate to heat gain?
o: Heat gain depends only on window color, not size
Larger windows always reduce heat gain
Window area has no effect on heat gain
The bigger the window area, the larger the heat gain
n: For windows, area matters: the bigger the area, the larger the heat gain.

q: Which term refers to a line of longitude that is important for determining solar noon at a given location?
o: Azimuth
Latitude
Meridian
Altitude
n: A Meridian is a line of longitude; important for determining solar noon at a given location.

q: According to the source's discussion of the uneven heating of the earth, what happens because the equator receives more solar energy than the poles?
o: Warm air at the equator sinks while cold air at the poles rises
Air pressure remains equal everywhere on Earth
The Coriolis effect eliminates any pressure gradient
Warm air at the equator rises (low pressure) while cold air at the poles sinks (high pressure), creating pressure gradients that drive air movement
n: The equator receives more solar energy than the poles. Warm air at the equator rises (low pressure), while cold air at the poles sinks (high pressure). This creates pressure gradients that drive air movement.

s: Problems in Areas with Tropical Climates
q: Which of the following is listed as a problem in areas with tropical climates?
o: High temperature, high humidity, slow wind velocities, and high precipitation levels during rainy days
Consistently cool temperatures year-round
An absence of insects and rodents
Low humidity levels and fast wind velocities
n: Problems in areas with tropical climates include high temperature level (heat), high humidity levels, slow wind velocities, high precipitation levels during rainy days, high incidence of typhoons, and abundance of insects and rodents due to damp ground conditions.

q: What is Cross Ventilation?
o: A ventilation strategy that uses stack effect alone, without any wind pressure
A method for cooling only the roof cavity of a building
A ventilation strategy relying on wind pressure differences between opposite sides of a building to move air through a space, entering from a windward opening and exiting through a leeward opening
A ventilation strategy that works only in urban areas with no wind
n: Cross ventilation relies on wind pressure differences between opposite sides of a building to move air through a space. Air enters from a windward opening and exits through a leeward opening, creating a cooling breeze. It is highly effective in tropical climates with consistent wind patterns and when the building is oriented to catch prevailing winds.

q: What is a Solar Path Diagram (solar chart)?
o: A geographic coordinate specifying north-south position
A diagram plotting the sun's path across the sky over the year, aiding in building orientation and shading design
The average solar radiation received outside Earth's atmosphere
A line of longitude important for solar noon
n: A Solar Path Diagram (Solar chart) is a diagram plotting the sun's path across the sky over the year, aiding in building orientation and shading design.

q: Which atmospheric circulation cell (60°–90° latitude) has cold air sinking at the poles and flowing equatorward?
o: Ferrel Cell
Hadley Cell
Polar Cell
Coriolis Cell
n: The Polar Cell (60°–90° latitude) has cold air sinking at the poles and flowing equatorward.

q: According to the source's Passive Systems table, which combination describes the cool climate strategy?
o: Maximum wind exposure and minimum thermal retention
Maximum thermal retention, maximum radiant heat gain, and maximum wind resistance
Minimum radiant heat gain and moderate internal airflow
Moderate thermal retention and slight wind exposure
n: For a cool climate, passive systems call for maximum thermal retention, maximum radiant heat gain, and maximum wind resistance.

s: Night Ventilation of Thermal Mass (Night Purging)
q: What is Night Ventilation of Thermal Mass (Night Purging)?
o: Sealing a building at night to trap daytime heat for use the following morning
A mechanical air-conditioning process used only during the day
A process that only works in climates with no temperature difference between day and night
Drawing cooler outdoor air into a building at night to flush out the day's accumulated heat from thermal mass such as walls and floors, preparing the building to stay cooler the next day
n: At night, cooler outdoor air is drawn into the building to flush out the day's accumulated heat from thermal mass (e.g., walls and floors). This prepares the building to stay cooler the next day. It is a sustainable, environmentally friendly cooling method relying on natural ventilation rather than energy-intensive air conditioning, and is very effective in climates with high daytime temperatures but cooler nights. It works best with good daytime shading and cross ventilation.

q: According to the source, Metropolitan Manila would generally be at what latitude?
o: 0 deg. (Equator)
14.5 deg. N
23.5 deg. N
66.5 deg. N
n: Metropolitan Manila would generally be in the 14.5 deg. N latitude.

s: Wind Flows Due to Heat Exchange
q: According to the source, what characteristic of air explains why wind flows due to heat exchange?
o: Air temperature changes more slowly than ground temperature
Air only moves due to the Coriolis effect
Air cannot transport temperature at all
Air has the ability to transport temperature, and its temperature changes faster than the ground temperature
n: Air has the ability to transport temperature. One characteristic of air is that its temperature changes faster than the ground temperature.

q: What is a Trombe Wall?
o: A mound or bank of earth used in landscaping
An outdoor platform designed for relaxation or solar access
A room with extensive glass surfaces designed to capture sunlight
A passive solar building design feature consisting of a thick wall painted dark and faced with glass, which absorbs solar heat and radiates it into the building
n: A Trombe Wall is a passive solar building design feature consisting of a thick wall painted dark and faced with glass, which absorbs solar heat and radiates it into the building.

q: In the Bahay Kubo, what are Sawali Walls, part of the Permeable Building Envelope?
o: Massive wooden trunks that elevate the living area
Woven bamboo or rattan panels that permit air filtration
Spaced bamboo flooring for ventilation and cleaning
Steeply pitched thatch roofs
n: Sawali Walls are woven bamboo or rattan panels that permit air filtration, as part of the Bahay Kubo's Permeable Building Envelope.

q: What are the three processes by which heat, a form of energy generated by the random motion of molecules, is transmitted?
o: Insulation, ventilation, and infiltration
Conduction, convection, and radiation
Radiation, refraction, and reflection
Absorption, emission, and diffusion
n: Heat is a form of energy generated by the random motion of molecules. There are three processes by which heat is transmitted: conduction, convection, and radiation.

q: According to the source, air enters a building through openings in the positive pressure zone and exits through openings in which zone?
o: There is no relationship between pressure zone and air entry/exit
Another positive pressure zone
Only the roof vents
The negative pressure zone
n: Air enters the building through openings located in the positive pressure zone and exits through openings located at the negative pressure zone.

q: What is a Shutter Panel?
o: A device or structure that blocks or filters sunlight
A solid or louvered panel that can be closed over windows to control light and heat
A mesh or fabric installed over windows to reduce solar heat gain
An adjustable window covering that can be tilted to control light and privacy
n: A Shutter Panel is a solid or louvered panel that can be closed over windows to control light and heat.

q: In the Bahay na Bato, what do the wide eaves (alero) provide, along with latticed vents fitted beneath them?
o: A location for solar collectors
A space designed to have no ventilation at all
The necessary sun shading for window openings, while the latticed vents underneath allow breeze to enter the roof cavity
Structural support for the stone ground floor only
n: The wide eaves (alero) provide the necessary sun shading for window openings, and the underside of the wide eaves has fitted latticed vents that allow breeze to enter the roof cavity.

q: Which heat transfer process is the transfer of heat through space by electro-magnetic waves, measured as temperature at the surface of the material, and is how the earth receives its heat from the sun?
o: Conduction
Convection
Solar Constant
Radiation
n: Radiation is the transfer of heat through a space by electro-magnetic waves and is measured as temperature at the surface of the material. The earth receives its heat from the sun by radiation.

q: According to the source, what happens when vertical wall projections (vertical deflectors) are placed parallel to the incident wind?
o: They only work when placed perpendicular to the main flow
They have no effect on airflow
They prevent wind shadows or dead zones of air
They create a wind shadow
n: Vertical deflectors — vertical wall projections placed parallel to the incident wind — prevent wind shadows or dead zones of air. But when placed perpendicular to the main flow, the same system can create a wind shadow. Placing openings at the foot of partitions will induce air flow.

q: According to the source, what may cause visual discomfort to a person directly facing a sunlit window, and how can this be eliminated?
o: Glare; eliminated when sun control devices are provided
Excess humidity; eliminated by using a solar screen
Excess ventilation; eliminated by closing all windows
Excess absorptivity; eliminated by painting the wall dark
n: To a person directly facing a sunlit window, visual discomfort may be due to glare. When sun control devices are provided, glare would be eliminated.

q: What is a Concha in the Bahay na Bato?
o: A sliding panel beneath a window sill
Latticework panels that framed the translucent capiz shells, used to completely shut windows at night or during a storm
An overhanging gallery protecting the ground floor
A pierced wooden panel above a doorway
n: Concha are latticework panels that framed the translucent capiz shells; they were used to completely shut windows at night or during a storm.

q: What is Solar Energy, as defined in the source?
o: A device that absorbs solar radiation and transfers the heat to a fluid
A house designed to harness solar energy for heating, lighting, or power
The average solar radiation received outside Earth's atmosphere
Radiant energy from the sun, essential for natural lighting, heating, and renewable energy systems in buildings
n: Solar Energy is radiant energy from the sun, essential for natural lighting, heating, and renewable energy systems in buildings.

q: According to PAGASA, what is the Philippine Northeast Monsoon season, occurring from November to February and bringing cool, dry air?
o: Tag-init
Habagat
Southwest Monsoon
Amihan
n: Amihan (Northeast Monsoon) occurs from November to February and brings cool, dry air.

q: What is the Venturi Effect?
o: The deflection of moving air due to Earth's rotation
The tendency of warm air to rise due to lower density
A principle where air slows down when passing through a narrow or constricted space, causing a pressure increase

A principle in fluid dynamics where air speeds up when it flows through a narrow or constricted space, causing a drop in pressure in that area — used to enhance natural ventilation through tapered corridors or narrow openings
n: The Venturi Effect is a principle in fluid dynamics where air (or fluid) speeds up when it flows through a narrow or constricted space, causing a drop in pressure in that area. In architecture, it can be intentionally used to enhance natural ventilation by guiding wind through narrow openings or tapered corridors, increasing airflow speed and helping draw air through indoor spaces.

q: According to the source, how is the Stack Effect (Natural Buoyancy) achieved as a modern passive cooling principle, using high-pitched roofs and open transoms (espejitos)?
o: Hot air is allowed to rise and escape through the roof ridge, pulling cooler air in through lower openings like the ventanillas
Hot air is trapped at the roof ridge with no escape, cooling the interior by radiation alone
Cool air is pumped mechanically from the roof ridge to the ground floor
The roof pitch has no effect on air movement, only the wall material does
n: Stack Effect (Natural Buoyancy): By using high-pitched roofs and open transoms (espejitos), hot air is allowed to rise and escape through the roof ridge, pulling cooler air in through lower openings like the ventanillas.

q: What distinguishes an Active Solar-Heating System, as illustrated by the solar collector, water tank, pump, and boiler diagram?
o: It utilizes building orientation, materials, and thermal mass to collect and distribute heat naturally
It relies entirely on radiation with no fluid transfer
It uses mechanical equipment like pumps or fans to circulate heat-transfer fluids
It only functions at night
n: An Active Solar-Heating System uses mechanical equipment like pumps or fans to circulate heat-transfer fluids.

q: According to the source's discussion of wind patterns, what does Amihan bring, and why is it good for natural ventilation design?
o: Cool, dry air from the northeast
Hot, humid air from the equator
No wind at all, only stillness
Warm, moist air from the southwest, bringing heavier rains and humidity
n: Amihan brings cool, dry air from the northeast, which is good for natural ventilation design.

q: According to the source's ranking of window shading coefficients from least to most desirable, which is ranked most desirable?
o: Reflective glass
Double glass
Window with awning
Clear glass with blinds
n: The source ranks shading coefficient of window types from least to most desirable as: 1. Double glass, 2. Clear glass with blinds, 3. Reflective glass, 4. Window with awning (most desirable).

q: Which method precisely calculates solar angles (azimuth and altitude) using spherical trigonometry, useful for detailed architectural analysis and design?
o: Solar Path Diagram
Solar Constant
Meridian
Sun Path
n: Sun Path refers to solar angles made up of azimuth and altitude, which can be precisely calculated by methods of spherical trigonometry — useful when detailed solar position and angles are required for architectural analysis and design.

q: Due to Earth's rotation, the Coriolis Effect deflects moving air to the right in the Northern Hemisphere. In which direction is it deflected in the Southern Hemisphere?
o: Also to the right
To the left
There is no deflection in the Southern Hemisphere
Straight upward
n: Due to Earth's rotation, moving air is deflected to the right in the Northern Hemisphere and to the left in the Southern Hemisphere. This deflection shapes wind patterns and circulation cells.

q: Which of the following is listed among the Design Objectives in Tropical Climates?
o: Maximize heat gain and minimize drainage
Eliminate all natural daylight from interior spaces
Minimize ventilation and maximize humidity levels
Maximize heat gain, maximize ventilation (while protecting from typhoon wind), prevent unnecessary increase in humidity, have good drainage, and protect spaces from insects and rodents
n: Design Objectives in Tropical Climates include: maximize heat gain (loss); maximize ventilation but protect from typhoon wind; prevent unnecessary increase in humidity levels; have a good drainage system to accommodate high annual precipitation; and protect spaces from insects and rodents.

q: According to the source, how can Cross Ventilation be achieved in building design?
o: By eliminating interior transoms and open floor plans
By placing all openings on a single wall only
By sealing all windows and relying solely on mechanical ventilation
By positioning windows, vents, or doors on opposite or adjacent walls to allow airflow across rooms, using louvered or operable windows and open floor plans or interior transoms
n: Cross ventilation can be achieved by positioning windows, vents, or doors on opposite or adjacent walls to allow airflow across rooms. Louvered or operable windows help regulate air entry and exit. Open floor plans or interior transoms allow airflow between rooms.

q: Which geographic coordinate specifies north-south position and influences solar angles and daylight length?
o: Azimuth
Meridian
Latitude
Longitude
n: Latitude is a geographic coordinate specifying north-south position, which influences solar angles and daylight length.

s: Principles of Air Flow — Pressure Gradient
q: Which of the following is one of the Principles of Air Flow listed in the source?
o: Air pressure has no bearing on air movement
Air flows from a low-pressure to a high-pressure area
Air always flows against the wind's initial direction
Air flows from a high-pressure to a low-pressure area
n: One principle of air flow is that air flows from a high-pressure to a low-pressure area.

q: According to the source's Passive Systems table, which combination describes the temperate climate strategy?
o: Moderate thermal retention, moderate radiant heat gain, slight wind exposure (humidity control), and moderate internal airflow
Maximum wind exposure and minimum radiant heat gain
Maximum thermal retention and maximum wind resistance
Minimum radiant heat gain only, with no airflow consideration
n: For a temperate climate, passive systems call for moderate thermal retention, moderate radiant heat gain, slight wind exposure (humidity control), and moderate internal airflow.

q: According to the source, what is the 'diurnal swing,' and why must it be high for thermal mass to be an effective passive strategy?
o: The amount of solar radiation absorbed by a black body over 24 hours
The angle between azimuth and altitude at solar noon
The difference between daytime and nighttime outdoor temperatures — it must be high for thermal mass to be effective for passive cooling and heating
The difference between summer and winter solar altitude — it has no relation to thermal mass
n: Diurnal swing is the difference between daytime and nighttime outdoor temperatures. This must be high for thermal mass to be an effective passive cooling and heating strategy; thermal mass can be used with nocturnal convective cooling or 'night cooling' to passively cool buildings.

q: What is the Summer Solstice?
o: The day when the sun reaches its highest point in the sky at noon, resulting in the longest day of the year, typically around June 21 in the Northern Hemisphere
A line of longitude important for solar noon
A day when day and night are approximately equal in length
The day when the sun reaches its lowest point in the sky at noon, resulting in the shortest day
n: The Summer Solstice is the day when the sun reaches its highest point in the sky at noon, resulting in the longest day of the year, typically around June 21 in the Northern Hemisphere.

q: What is a Sea Breeze?
o: The deflection of air due to the Coriolis effect
A wind pattern found only at the poles
Wind that develops as daytime heating begins: the land warms more rapidly than the water, causing a seaward movement of air upward, with wind directed from the sea toward land
Wind that develops at night when land cools faster than water, moving from land to sea
n: A Sea Breeze occurs as daytime heating begins: the land warms more rapidly than the water. Upward expansion of the air column over the land causes a seaward movement of air upward, and wind from the sea directed toward land develops.

q: What is a Solarium / Sunroom?
o: A mound or bank of earth used for insulation
An outdoor platform designed to receive ample sunlight
A thermal mass wall designed to absorb and store solar heat
A room with extensive glass surfaces designed to capture sunlight for warmth and light
n: A Solarium / Sunroom is a room with extensive glass surfaces designed to capture sunlight for warmth and light.
